chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a tree that a man uproots in his house within the Haram (sanctuary), he said: 'If he built the house and the tree was in it, he is not allowed to uproot it; and if it sprouted in his house and he owned it, he should uproot it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on uprooting a tree in one's house within the Haram if the tree was there before or after the house was built?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal distinction between pre-existing natural features and later growth within the Haram's residential zones, emphasizing that ownership rights determine the permissibility of uprooting. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the sanctity of the Haram does not automatically preserve all vegetation if it interferes with the owner's established property rights, provided the tree was not present at the time of construction. This ruling is crucial for understanding the practical application of Haram boundaries in historical and contemporary contexts.
